name: Nude / white waterline eyeliner

lead: Nude or white waterline eyeliner is a makeup technique where a light, skin-toned or white pencil is applied to the inner rim of the lower lid. The payoff is eyes that look brighter, larger and more awake.

The light colour counters the darker, redder rim of the lower lid, so shadow and redness at the lid margin recede and the eye appears more open. It belongs to the long tradition of eyeliner, which dates to ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia. No study has tested its effect on perceived attractiveness or eye size.

paras: Users tightline or drag the pencil along the inner lower rim after drying the area, usually as a finishing step in a daily makeup routine, sometimes paired with mascara or a darker upper liner.

Anything applied to the waterline touches the eye surface; waterproof, eye-safe products are generally preferred per general makeup references. Shared or old pencils can carry bacteria. No studies of waterline-specific harms were found.

angle.text: A nude or white pencil on the lower waterline reduces the dark, red rim contrast and makes the eyes look brighter, larger and more awake as soon as it is applied. It is a popular makeup technique rather than a studied one.

lead: Nude or white waterline eyeliner is a makeup practice in which a light-colored (skin-toned, beige or white) pencil is applied to the lower waterline, the inner rim of the lower eyelid. Practitioners in appearance communities say it makes the eyes look brighter, more awake and larger.

It belongs to the broader tradition of eyeliner, which dates to ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia.[1] Published research on the cosmetic effect of light waterline liner is limited; no clinical study of its effect on perceived attractiveness or eye size was found.
infobox: Light-colored eye pencil or gel liner

paras: The technique places a pale pencil along the lower waterline, in contrast to the dark liner traditionally used for definition. Wikipedia describes the related practice of tight lining, which sits against the waterline and makes lashes seem to begin farther back on the lid, and notes that waterproof products are generally preferred because of the eye's sensitive surface.[1]

Proponents describe the effect as reducing the look of redness or tiredness at the lid margin and visually enlarging the eye. These are claims made by users; the sources reviewed do not quantify them.
Products placed on the waterline contact the eye surface. The sources consulted do not discuss infection or irritation rates for waterline liner specifically.

No studies found. A pediatric dermatology report described using a white eyeliner pencil to mark capillary malformations before laser treatment, a medical use unrelated to cosmetic eye brightening.[2]
